steps.body: Subtraction also works place by place. When every top digit is big enough, each column subtracts on its own.
steps.narration: Subtraction also works place by place. When every top digit is big enough, each column subtracts on its own.

widget.prompt: Build what remains: 568 take away 234 leaves this number.

commonBuilds.feedback: That kept all 8 ones — but 4 of them were taken away, leaving 4.

widget.missFeedback: That build names a different number — total each unit's worth and match 334 exactly.
widget.successFeedback: 3 flats, 3 rods, 4 cubes — each place gave up its own share.

predict.prompt: 568 − 234: does any column need a trade?

options.label: No — every top digit is bigger

predict.reveal: 8≥4, 6≥3, 5≥2 — each column can pay from its own supply. The places only have to talk when a top digit comes up short; that conversation is called trading.

cml.actionGoal: Manipulate the model and track how it represents g2b sub no trade.
invariants: Trading between places changes the FORM of a quantity, never its value — the model and the number must stay equal for g2b sub no trade.
misconceptions: Treating a trade as adding or removing amount instead of renaming the same total.
cml.counterfactualPrompt: What change would make the blocks stop matching the written number?

explanationVariants: Each column pays its own bill.

commonErrors.feedback: That joined the two amounts; taking away calls for subtraction.
A ten slipped back in — subtract each place carefully.

widget.fallbackFeedback: Line the places up — hundreds with hundreds, tens with tens, ones with ones — and work one column at a time.

hints: Line up hundreds, tens, and ones.
Work one place at a time.
Carry every trade into its column.

widget.prompt: Before computing 477 + 244, about how big should the answer be?

options.label: About 700 — round each and add
options.feedback: Correct — rounding to hundreds gives roughly 700, a quick sanity check on the exact sum.

options.label: About 1000
options.feedback: That estimate sits hundreds too high; rounding each addend keeps the check honest.

options.label: Exactly 721 — estimates must be exact
options.feedback: An estimate trades exactness for speed on purpose; the exact sum is the second step.

options.label: No estimate is possible before solving
options.feedback: Rounding first is precisely how you predict the size of an answer before working it.
